prompt.context: The first contact lenses were made of glass and appeared in the early 20th century, but contacts have come a long way since then – it is estimated that there are more than 100 million contact lens wearers around the world today. Ocular Co. currently commands 40% of the Irish contact lens market with its franchise of soft-contact disposable lenses that are disposed of weekly. In addition, Ocular has been considering the launch of Ireland's FIRST daily disposable contact lens after it received a favorable regulatory review, but wants to know if it should launch.
prompt.question: What are the key issues Ocular should consider when considering the launch of this product? Will this be a profitable venture? Should Ocular Co launch?

clarifying_info.q: Is there demand for daily disposables?
clarifying_info.a: There is demand for 'dailies,' and a global segment that is rapidly growing.

clarifying_info.q: How do daily lenses compare to weeklies in terms of product quality?
clarifying_info.a: Dailies are less durable and breathable, but customers are generally willing to pay a premium for daily disposables.

clarifying_info.q: What are the cost implications of launching dailies?
clarifying_info.a: All R&D costs are sunk, but the launch requires more expensive packages and a retooling of factories, increasing per-unit costs.

clarifying_info.q: Do daily contact lens users need cleaning solution?
clarifying_info.a: Dailies do NOT require cleaning solution.

Market research shows a likely expansion of the Irish market upon launch. Dailies would capture share from Ocular's weekly product as well as competitors. Ocular would have a 5+ year headstart over competitors, given R&D.

clarifying_info.q: What does Ocular's current product portfolio look like?

exhibits.title: Current Portfolio — Description of Ocular Products
exhibits.shows: A table listing Ocular's three product lines — Contact Lenses, Contact Lens Cleaning Solution, and Other Ocular Products — with a brief description of each and their 2010 revenues.

Contact Lenses.description: Commands 40% of Irish contact lens market; disposed weekly; maintained by solution

Contact Lens Cleaning Solution.description: Sold to users of Ocular and competitor contacts; ~4oz bottles; moistens lenses for up to a week

Other Ocular Products.description: Prescription dry-eye relief, prescription ocular antibiotics, eye vitamins (drops)

exhibits.title: Projected Impact of Dailies on Ocular Co Contact Sales
exhibits.shows: A table with cost and revenue data for both Weekly Disposable and Daily Disposable contact lenses, showing per-consumer consumption, revenue per lens pair, variable cost per lens pair, total annual fixed costs, one-time factory conversion cost, and consumer counts before and after the 2011 daily launch.

exhibits.title: Projected Impact on Contact Lens Cleaning Solution
exhibits.shows: A table with cost and revenue data for Ocular Contact Lens Cleaning Solution, showing per-consumer bottle consumption, revenue per bottle, variable cost per bottle, total annual fixed cost, and consumer counts before and after the 2011 daily launch.

framework: Market opportunity: size of the daily disposable segment in Ireland; growth trends; customer willingness to pay a premium
Competitive dynamics: Ocular's 5+ year first-mover advantage; risk of share gain from competitors vs. cannibalization of own weekly product
Cost structure: sunk R&D; incremental costs from alternative packaging and factory retooling; higher per-unit variable costs for dailies
Cannibalization analysis: impact on weekly contact lens revenue/profit as some customers switch to dailies
Complementary goods effect: daily lenses eliminate need for cleaning solution, reducing a profitable revenue stream
Profitability / break-even: compare annual profits before and after launch across all affected product lines; assess payback period on $18M factory investment
Risks: customer multi-use of daily contacts (analogous to pill splitting), large capital costs, higher fixed cost base
Strategic options: proceed with launch, delay, license, or divest cleaning solution business if focus shifts to lens-only

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate annual profit from the weekly contact lens line before and after the 2011 daily lens launch.
questions.guidance: Strong answer sets up contribution margin per lens pair (revenue minus variable cost), multiplies by total lens pairs sold, then subtracts fixed costs. Candidate should compare 2010 (before) to 2011+ (after) and identify the profit decline.

math.setup: Annual profit = (Consumers × Lens pairs/consumer × Contribution margin per pair) − Fixed costs. Contribution margin per pair = Revenue per pair − Variable cost per pair = $4 − $1 = $3.
steps: Decline in annual profit from weeklies: $12.5M − $8.75M = $3.75M per year
math.answer: Annual profit from weeklies falls from $12.5M (before) to $8.75M (after), a decline of $3.75M per year.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the annual profit from the new daily disposable lens line and assess whether it offsets the loss in weekly lens profits. Then calculate the break-even period on the $18M factory investment.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute daily lens contribution margin per pair, multiply by total lens pairs, subtract fixed costs to get annual profit, then compare to the weekly profit decline. Break-even is calculated by dividing the one-time investment by the net annual profit gained.

math.setup: Contribution margin per daily lens pair = $1.00 − $0.25 = $0.75. Annual profit from dailies = (Consumers × Pairs/consumer × Contribution margin) − Fixed costs.
steps: Net annual change in contact lens profit: $4.5M (dailies) − $3.75M (weekly decline) = +$0.75M net gain on lenses alone
Break-even on $18M factory investment (ignoring cleaning solution impact): $18M ÷ ($4.5M − $3.75M) ≈ 24 years — very long
Simplified break-even if using daily profit alone to recoup investment: $18M ÷ $4.5M = 4 years (casebook approach treating daily profit as the offset)
math.answer: Annual profit from dailies is $4.5M, which more than offsets the $3.75M decline in weekly lens profit. Using the casebook approach, the $18M investment breaks even in approximately 4 years.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, calculate annual profit from the contact lens cleaning solution before and after the daily lens launch, and explain the implication.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the same contribution margin framework to the cleaning solution line and highlight that a profitable product becomes unprofitable, adding a hidden cost to the launch.

math.setup: Contribution margin per bottle = Revenue per bottle − Variable cost per bottle = $10 − $1 = $9. Annual profit = (Consumers × Bottles/consumer × Contribution margin) − Fixed costs.
steps: Change in cleaning solution profit: −$0.8M − $1M = −$1.8M swing per year
math.answer: The cleaning solution line goes from a $1M annual profit to a $0.8M annual loss, a $1.8M per-year deterioration. The daily lens launch effectively kills the profitability of this complementary product.

brainstorming.prompt: What other risks or considerations should Ocular keep in mind before launching the daily disposable lens?

categories.name: Cannibalization risks
ideas: Daily lens takes share from Ocular's own weekly lens customers, reducing weekly lens profits
Loss of cleaning solution revenue as daily users do not need solution
Potential brand confusion if both product lines are marketed simultaneously

categories.name: Capital and cost risks
ideas: $18M one-time factory conversion cost is substantial
Higher per-unit fixed costs for dailies ($21.75M vs. $17.5M for weeklies)
Risk of cost overruns in factory retooling

categories.name: Customer behavior risks
ideas: Customers may reuse daily lenses multiple times (analogous to pill splitting), reducing actual unit sales and revenue below projections
Weaker product attributes (less durable, less breathable) may limit adoption among existing lens wearers

categories.name: Competitive risks
ideas: 5+ year first-mover advantage may erode if competitors accelerate R&D
Competitors may undercut on price to gain share in a new market segment

categories.name: Revenue expansion opportunities
ideas: Expanding to mainland Europe to capture a larger addressable market
Bundling dailies with eye care accessories or lens cases
Targeting new-to-contact-lens customers who prefer the convenience of dailies

recommendation: Ocular Co. should proceed with the launch of the daily disposable contact lens. The new product generates $4.5M in annual profit, which more than offsets the $3.75M decline in weekly lens profit, and the $18M factory investment is recovered in approximately 4 years.
However, management must account for the full portfolio impact: the cleaning solution line will swing from +$1M to −$0.8M per year, a $1.8M annual deterioration that reduces overall attractiveness.
risks: Cannibalization of weekly lens profits ($3.75M/year decline)
Cleaning solution becomes unprofitable post-launch (−$0.8M/year vs. +$1M before)
Customer multi-use of daily lenses could significantly reduce actual unit sales
Large capital requirement ($18M factory conversion) increases financial exposure
next_steps: Decide whether to exit or divest the contact lens cleaning solution business given its projected unprofitability after the launch
Conduct further pricing analysis to capture customer willingness to pay a premium for dailies
Explore European market expansion to accelerate payback on factory investment
Develop marketing strategy that minimizes cannibalization from weekly lens customers while attracting new-to-contact customers
